rationale: ENTRYPOINTS ONLY. This manifest answers exactly one question: from where does a runtime reachability walk start. It is NOT the source universe and NOT an eligibility filter - see .quality/policy/source-universe.json for which files quality tooling may inspect, and which analyzers may inspect them. This file previously carried an `exclude` list and served as scope authority, which dropped globals.d.ts and scripts/quality/fixtures/* from analysis because nothing imports them at runtime. Those files are read critically and carry accepted findings; they were never runtime artifacts, not unreachable code. Widening, narrowing or removing a root here changes what reachability can conclude and is hashed into policyDigest, so it invalidates accepted baselines.

roots.proof: package.json main is src/entrypoints/cli.tsx, and bin maps `claude` to dist/cli.js which scripts/build.ts produces from src/entrypoints/cli.tsx via bun build --root=src/entrypoints.
package.json script `build` runs `bun run scripts/build.ts`; it is the producer of the shipped bundle.
The model gateway process itself; spawned by the supervisor chain and by scripts/gateway-deepseek.ps1.
package.json script `quality` runs `bun run scripts/quality/cli.ts`; it is the runtime entrypoint of the quality tooling.
Every fixture spec is executed by `bun test scripts/quality/fixtures` (package.json quality:test); they are runtime code for the quality harness even though they live in a fixture directory.
